newsitem.title: USA: Reader's profits drop, to invest in publishing, promotion.
newsitem.headline: Reader's profits drop, to invest in publishing, promotion.

text.p: Reader's Digest Association Inc., reporting a sharp drop in quarterly earnings, said Wednesday it will invest up to $400 million over four years in more aggressive publishing and promotion initiatives.
Reader's Digest also said its net income fell 33 percent to $37.6 million, or 35 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 31 from $55.8 million, or 51 cents a share, in the year-ago period.
The company's stock lost $1.25, or almost 5 percent, to $24.75 in morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

Reader's Digest said its revenues for the quarter fell 8 percent to $684.3 million from $747.5 million, as higher circulation in the Pacific and other markets were offset by decreases in Europe and the United States.
Lower revenues, increased promotion spending and investments in new countries reduced operating profit significantly, the company said.
The company said its new investment programme was intended to increase the size and value of the company's global customer base by capturing a larger share of the growing markets for its products.

With the investment initiative, the company said, it expects earnings next year to decline as it begins to stabilise and build its customer base, produce growth and maximize the value of its global franchise.
The Pleasantville, N.Y.-based publisher said it expects full-year fiscal 1997 earnings of about $1.70 per share, excluding any fourth-quarter charges from the investment plan.
It said it expects to record one-time charges in the fourth quarter of up to $100 million.
